title: Selectively build TFLite for IOS failure
body: I am building TensorFlow Lite 2.11.0 from source on macOS Monterey 12.6.2 with Python 3.9, Bazel 5.3.0, and compiler 14.0.0. I reproduced this with TensorFlow nightly. Following the selective iOS framework guide with a model that uses builtin and select ops fails while compiling the generated custom C API registration because tensorflow/lite/core/shims/builtin_ops_list.inc is an undeclared inclusion. Adding shims:builtin_ops_list has not fixed the build.

symptoms_visible: My selective iOS framework build stops while compiling custom_c_api_registration_registration.cc because builtin_ops_list.inc is reported as an undeclared inclusion.
Adding the builtin_ops_list dependency has not made the build complete.
N0.label: N0 selective iOS build failure reported

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the same undeclared-inclusion failure by configuring TensorFlow for iOS and running build_frameworks.sh with the attached toy model for x86_64, armv7, and arm64.
The same failure is reproducible on another Mac with Bazel 5.3.0.
N1.label: N1 reproduction established

symptoms_visible: After adding the proposed deps block to build_frameworks.sh, the same build command gets past the earlier point but stops with a different build error.
N2_x.label: N2_x dependency-only patch aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating the repository and rerunning the command, Bazel says target TensorFlowLiteC_framework is not declared in tensorflow/lite/ios/tmp.
N3_x.label: N3_x first merged update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The generated tmp/BUILD file contains a TensorFlowLiteC_framework target, but the custom library declaration uses tflite_custom_c_library.
N4.label: N4 generated BUILD inspected

symptoms_visible: After changing build_frameworks.sh to use tflite_custom_cc_library, the earlier undeclared-inclusion and missing-target error is gone.
My build then stops later while producing libtensorflow_framework.2.dylib for TensorFlowLiteSelectTfOps_framework, so I have not completed a successful full build on my machine.
N_terminal.label: terminal original script defect corrected but full reporter build unverified

question_patterns: Can you provide a toy model and the exact steps and command needed to reproduce the failure?
What configure choices and build_frameworks.sh arguments reproduce this?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached the toy model. I fetch the TensorFlow repository, run ./configure with iOS enabled and the other options disabled, copy the model into the repository, and run: bash tensorflow/lite/ios/build_frameworks.sh --input_models=toy_tflite_model_20230308.tflite --target_archs=x86_64,armv7,arm64. That produces the undeclared-inclusion error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The toy model builds successfully; the failure only occurs with my private model containing a custom operator.
The same toy model and command fail when I omit x86_64 and build only arm64.

edges.comment: From c0-c2. The reporter supplied the toy model, configure procedure, command, and log in c1. Participant1 independently reproduced the same opening failure on a Mac M1 with Bazel 5.3.0 in c2; that affected test run is folded into the simulated user side, and its screenshot is attached to N1.

solution.intent: Patch the generated custom-library declaration in build_frameworks.sh by adding the builtin_ops_list target to its deps block.
solution.concrete_example: Add a deps block containing //tensorflow/lite/core/shims:builtin_ops_list to the generated custom library in tensorflow/lite/ios/build_frameworks.sh, then rerun the selective build.

edges.comment: From c6-c7 on the reporter's macOS iOS build. The reporter applied the exact generated deps snippet requested by the maintainer and reported a different build failure, so adding only the dependency was not the complete fix.

solution.intent: Pull the maintainer's first merged update to the outdated iOS framework script and rerun the selective framework command.
solution.concrete_example: Update to the newly merged build_frameworks.sh change and rerun the same command with the toy model.

edges.comment: From c9-c10 on the reporter's system. The maintainer said the first change was merged and locally verified, but after pulling it the reporter received the observable error that TensorFlowLiteC_framework was not declared. This first update was therefore not the final accepted correction.

question_patterns: Can you inspect or paste the generated tensorflow/lite/ios/tmp/BUILD file?
Does the generated tmp/BUILD file contain the expected framework declaration, and what custom-library rule does it use?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked tensorflow/lite/ios/tmp/BUILD. It does contain ios_static_framework(name = "TensorFlowLiteC_framework", ...), and its custom library block is tflite_custom_c_library(name = "custom_c_api", deps = ["//tensorflow/lite/core/shims:builtin_ops_list"], models = ["toy_tflite_model_20230308.tflite"]).

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The generated tmp/BUILD file is empty and contains neither a custom library nor a TensorFlowLiteC_framework declaration.
The same declarations are present, but the model appears under a differently named file.

edges.comment: From c11-c14. On the reporter's macOS checkout, the maintainer asked for the generated BUILD content and the reporter pasted it verbatim. The raw evidence shows the generated rule and target; identifying which rule helper is wrong remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct the outdated selective iOS generation path to use the C++ custom-library helper for a model containing select operations, merge that script correction, and have the reporter rerun the complete framework build.
solution.concrete_example: Replace tflite_custom_c_library with tflite_custom_cc_library in the generated selective-build rule in build_frameworks.sh, update to the corrected script, and rerun the same toy-model command. Confirm that the original registration and framework-target errors are gone, then separately diagnose any later TensorFlowLiteSelectTfOps_framework tooling failure.
solution.inference_hint: The final maintainer diagnosis in c15 is that the generated selective iOS rule must use tflite_custom_cc_library rather than tflite_custom_c_library. That conclusion is derived from the pasted BUILD content and the model's select operations; it was not supplied by the reporter. The later libtensorflow_framework.2.dylib/realpath failure is treated as a separate tooling issue, not as evidence against this script correction.

edges.comment: From c15-c25 and c27. The reporter changed to tflite_custom_cc_library and confirmed in c16 that the prior error disappeared, but then encountered a later SelectTfOps dylib genrule failure and filed it separately as issue 60088. Participant1 reported a successful framework build after the merges in c27, but that is relayed evidence from another operator, not the reporter's own full-build confirmation. The Android subproblem in c26-c28 is a different deployment and is deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: the selective iOS build_frameworks.sh path was outdated and generated tflite_custom_c_library where the model with select operations required tflite_custom_cc_library.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the reproduced toy-model build and the inspected generated tmp/BUILD content, not inferred from the undeclared-inclusion message alone.

Must not present adding only //tensorflow/lite/core/shims:builtin_ops_list or merely pulling the first merged script update as the complete fix; both were followed by further build errors on the reporter's system.

Must keep the later libtensorflow_framework.2.dylib/realpath failure separate from the original iOS script defect rather than replacing the final accepted diagnosis with a Python-version or configuration theory.

Must ask the reporter to verify the complete selective iOS framework build with the corrected script before declaring the reporter's environment fully resolved; the thread only confirms that the original error disappeared, while a different operator reported a successful full build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable TensorFlow source-build user who can configure Bazel builds, edit generated build rules and shell scripts, inspect BUILD files, update Python, and file a focused follow-up issue.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise but log-oriented; follows requested experiments, pastes exact commands and errors, and reports when each change moves the build to a new failure.
